units.mathematical_text: A randomized algorithm chooses its queries and stopping decisions as Borel functions of its internal randomness and previous oracle responses, where the randomness is independent of the input. Its output may be any \mathbb{R}^{d}-valued Borel function of the same information. The algorithm has fixed query budget T if it makes at most T queries for every admissible input and every realization of its internal randomness.

Its output may be any ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued Borel function of the same information. The algorithm has fixed query budget TT if it makes at most TT queries for every admissible input and every realization of its internal randomness.
